input.quote: 11.5 Special, Indirect, and Other Losses. EXCEPT (A) FOR FRAUD, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR GROSS NEGLIGENCE, (B) FOR A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS OBLIGATIONS UNDER [ARTICLE 9 OR SECTION 5.8], (C) AS PROVIDED UNDER [***] AND (D) TO THE EXTENT ANY SUCH DAMAGES ARE REQUIRED TO BE PAID TO A THIRD PARTY AS PART OF A CLAIM FOR WHICH A PARTY PROVIDES INDEMNIFICATION UNDER THIS ARTICLE 11, NEITHER PARTY NOR ANY OF ITS AFFILIATES SHALL BE LIABLE FOR INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, PUNITIVE OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES
input.rationale:
The Agreement contains no aggregate liability cap for either Party. Article 11 supplies mutual indemnities (Sections 11.1/11.2), a mutual all-caps exclusion of indirect and consequential damages with carve-outs for fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, breach of Article 9 or Section 5.8, and third-party indemnity pass-through (Section 11.5), and insurance minimums (Section 11.6). Searches for "aggregate liability", "shall not exceed", "limitation of liability", "maximum liability", "no event shall", "liable", "damages" and "Losses" return no cap; the only "maximum aggregate" figures are Article 6 milestone payment ceilings, not liability limits. Both fallback cap elements are therefore absent from the operative text, so the clause the rule expects is missing.

We have inserted a single new Section 11.7 at the end of Article 11 stating a mutual cap — "each Party's total aggregate liability ... shall not exceed the fees paid or payable by AbbVie under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" — at the fallback basis (no USD 1,000,000 floor is volunteered). Because the new cap would otherwise swallow currently unlimited exposures, the same sentence expressly places outside the cap each Party's indemnification obligations under Article 11, breaches of Article 9 (confidentiality) or Section 5.8 (Harpoon's exclusivity), and its fraud, wilful misconduct or gross negligence, mirroring the existing Section 11.5 exceptions. Placement at the end of Article 11 as Section 11.7 avoids renumbering Section 11.6 and creates no dangling cross-reference; Section 11.5 is left verbatim.

Note for the deal team: the cap is symmetric and preserves our recourse for indemnified and confidentiality claims, but it is a real change of risk allocation in a deal whose consideration is an upfront/option payment, Article 6 milestones and Net Sales royalties rather than recurring fees. If the business prefers to keep the mutually uncapped regime (which does not trigger any walk-away test), this edit can be dropped; if it is taken forward, we would also press to place AbbVie's Article 6 payment obligations and infringement of the other Party's intellectual property outside the cap, which is our preferred position.

proposal.summary: Insert a mutual aggregate liability cap based on 12 months of fees, with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct outside the cap.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a mutual aggregate liability cap set at the fees paid or payable by AbbVie in the twelve months preceding the claim, which is our fallback position; the Agreement currently contains no cap for either Party. Consistent with Section 11.5, each Party's indemnification obligations, breaches of Article 9 or Section 5.8, and its fraud, wilful misconduct or gross negligence sit outside the cap.

ops.text: 11.7 Limitation of Liability. Except for a Party's fraud, willful misconduct or gross negligence, a Party's breach of its obligations under Article 9 or Section 5.8, and a Party's indemnification obligations under this Article 11, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid or payable by AbbVie under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim.

mappings.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
